candidates.change_summary: Change the requirement that msg.value == 1 ether to require msg.value == 2 ether, causing lockInGuess to accept only 2 ETH and thus alter stored guesses for callers sending 1 ETH.
Remove the requirement that previous guess block is zero, allowing callers to overwrite an existing guess and thus change the post-call stored guess value.
Set the stored block to the current block instead of block.number + 1, changing the stored block value visible after the call.
Swap the order of assignments so block is set before guess, which can change observable state ordering if another contract reads in between (and affects reentrancy scenarios).
Clear any existing guess before setting new values, ensuring the post-call guess always equals the provided hash but temporarily sets guess to zero (affecting intermediate observable state).
Change comparison from strict equality of guess to comparing only the first 16 bytes (partial match), so winners differ when settle finishes.
Remove resetting guesses[msg.sender].block to 0 so settle leaves the block number intact, changing observed state after call.
Move the block reset to after the transfer so that if transfer reverts or fails, block may not be cleared (observable difference).
Invert the comparison so winners are those whose guess does NOT equal the answer, changing who receives funds and the state after settle.
Use blockhash of current block instead of the stored block number when computing answer, altering outcome and state observed after settle.
